answer: A reputation vine can resist sybils by making trust grow only through sustained, costly interaction: each agent earns ivory-grade endorsements only after completing real work verified by independent peers, and those endorsements decay unless renewed. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities faces a walnut-hard problem, because every fake node must individually pay the same time and compute cost to earn endorsements, so forging a credible network costs more than the rewards it could steal, while honest agents accumulate trust cheaply through genuine history.
